messages:
maya: quick Q — when we fuse dequant into the attn kernel (INT4/INT8/FP8 paths), what's our fallback story if the fused kernel hits an unsupported shape or alignment?

maya: e.g. seq_len 7, kv_cache partial, per-head scales not contiguous. Do we abort to a generic dequant+attn path or try a slower fused path? :thinking_face:

tom: good callout. current plan was: try fused kernel, if it returns STATUS_UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE then route to generic path (separate dequant -> matmul-attn). cheaper to implement for now.

ash: consequences: fallback implies extra memcpy/allocs for dequanted tensors. must make allocator decisions explicit. If we blindly fallback, tail lat spikes.

zara: can we instead provide a hybrid: fused-kernel that handles common shapes (multiple-of-8 heads, kv aligned) and a lightweight adapter that converts rare layouts to the fused-friendly layout with minimal copy?

oleg: adapter idea sounds promising. but note: converting layout for KV cache means we need to keep mapping metadata so subsequent requests reuse converted buffers. otherwise we pay conversion every call.

maya: agreed. propose: 1) fused kernel fast path, 2) cached-conversion path (convert once per cached-segment and store a weak ref), 3) generic fallback.

tom: +1. we should expose a runtime flag to force always-generic for debugging: --quant-attn-mode={auto,cached,force-generic}.

ash: small nit: cached-conversion increases memory footprint. we need a TTL policy and eviction linked to sequence ranges. also account for multi-tenant isolation (per-model cache).

zara: on quant specifics: FP8 path has per-tensor exponent metadata that we cannot drop. if fused kernel assumes per-head scale and FP8 shared exponent, it fails for dynamic exponent algorithms. we need API-level contract: what quant metadata the kernel expects.

oleg: yes — define a QuantLayout descriptor: data_type, per_head_scales?:bool, exponent_layout?:"global"|"per_channel"|"per_head", scale_dtype. That descriptor must be part of KernelCaps so kernel selector can match.

maya: sounds like a small RFC: add KernelCaps.quant_layout as part of selection key. Then routing can pick kernels that declare support for given QuantLayout.

tom: selection must be fast. do precompiled compatibility masks per model at load-time, not per request.

ash: test plan: generate fuzzed shapes + quant metadata matrix and assert outputs between fused and generic paths within tolerance. Add perf regression guards in CI.

ci-bot: perf benchmark job queued: "quant-attn-fusion-smoke". link: http://ci/jobs/1234

zara: runtime API question: should callers be able to opt-out of fusion for correctness? e.g., strict-determinism mode for evals.

maya: yes, add request-level flags: waive_fusion=true/false and a model-level default. Useful for A/B quality runs.

oleg: about KV cache: converted buffers complicate rollback during rollouts. when a canary model changes quant params we must invalidate cache conversions. tie conversions to (model_id, model_version, quant-checksum).

tom: additional trade: on GPU architectures with tensor cores, fused dequant+matmul has huge perf wins for INT8/INT4. we should add a perf heuristic: if expected tokens/sec > threshold, prefer fused even if conversion cost non-zero.

maya: action items:
- oleg: draft QuantLayout spec and cache key rules (ETA 2d)
- zara: enumerate FP8 exponent modes we see in model catalog (ETA 1d)
- tom: add runtime flag plumbing and precompiled kernel mask (ETA 3d)
- ash: design eviction/TTL for converted buffers (ETA 2d)
- maya: add CI fuzz test matrix and perf job (ETA 1d)

zara: also add a small note to docs: "When using fused quant-attn, some rare seq/kv shapes will route to a generic path; to guarantee identical outputs, use waive_fusion=false" (or reverse wording)

maya: thanks all. I'll open a follow-up thread with the mini-RFC and link to kernels repo.

tom: TY. feel free to @me on PRs. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: build passed for branch quant-attn-adapter (job 1256)
